newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1 Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1 Wednesday.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs were expected to be $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower on Wednesday as weak demand continued to weigh on the market, livestock dealers said.
"The runs have been light but demand has been poor and I would have to say they are going to try to take another $0.50 to $1.00 off it tomorrow," one Illinois dealer said.
One dealer in Indiana also noted cooler weather had led to a pick-up in runs in his area.
"We've got more hogs than we need. The kill is about full this week for us," he said.
Dealers said, however, the cash market may be close to bottoming with prices possibly starting to stabilise at around $57.00 to $57.50 per cwt for the key Iowa-south Minnesota area on Thursday.
USDA reported a top in Iowa-south Minnesota on Tuesday of $58.00 per cwt, a drop of $3.50 from a week earlier.
They noted producers were staying fairly current of marketings while hog weights remained light.
"It will come back but for now it is just a little bit cheaper," one Indiana dealer said.
